answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with throughput-scaled bonding. Each identity locks a bond in a vault that grows with the square of its declared work cap, so ten identities claiming the same total output must post far more collateral than one honest agent. A bridge between the registry and the payment ledger checks the bond before releasing reward. Identities that wander above their cap without topping up are paused and fined, so doubling fake identities quadruples locked capital while honest throughput stays cheap, and slashing takes the bond of any identity caught sharing work.
